title: They looked from Trinity to the blind columned porch of the bank of Ireland
html_source: if “they” refers to the women and their frankly-armed male companions, this suggests they were facing away from the college, and toward the bank. Additionally, if Artifoni is looking over Stephen’s shoulder, and can see the Oliver Goldsmith statue, and if the two men face each other, as is likely, that means that it is Artifoni who sees the statue and the the “carfuls of tourists,” and that Stephen sees only the “blind columned porch of the bank of Ireland,” and its roocoocooing pigeons. It also means that this is only the narrator’s voice, and is not from Stephen’s memory “bank”.

er at Goldsmith's knobby poll. 

 Two carfuls of tourists passed slowly, their women sitting fore, gripping the handrests. Palefaces. Men's arms frankly round their stunted forms.
anchor.suffix:
where pigeons roocoocooed. 

 — Anch'io ho avuto di queste idee Almidano Artifoni said quand' ero giovine come Lei. Eppoi mi sono convinto che il mondo è una bestia. È peccato. Pe
